Pinned core source resolves sysfs behavior: create_files removes files already created when one sysfs_create_group call fails; on normal unload, platform_device_unregister -> platform_device_del -> device_del -> kobject_del -> sysfs_remove_dir -> kernfs_remove deactivates nodes and drains active references. This establishes normal sysfs teardown ordering, not I/O mapping or OF-node release.

Pinned of_find_compatible_node returns a device_node with incremented refcount and requires of_node_put when done. The stock ftmmod corpus has no of_node_put call; pinned of_iomap maps the resource but does not put the node reference.

observations.claim: Pinned platform_device_register calls device_initialize before platform_device_add and explicitly requires platform_device_put on error, including when register returns failure. Stock init_module passes the ftm_dev object from .data, propagates registration failure as -ENODEV, and the module corpus has no platform_device_put call.
observations.locator: drivers/base/platform.c:768-781; init_module stock .init.text+0x28..0x34 and +0x74..0xa8; Ghidra symbols ftm_dev at .data base

observations.claim: Pinned __platform_driver_probe returns -ENODEV and unregisters the driver if no platform device binds; it does not unregister the platform device. Stock init_module propagates that error. Pinned do_init_module frees the module on negative init return and does not invoke cleanup_module on that failure path.

Normal module cleanup unregisters the platform device; pinned platform/sysfs/kernfs source follows platform_device_unregister -> platform_device_del -> device_del -> kobject_del -> sysfs_remove_dir -> kernfs_remove. kernfs marks nodes removing/deactivates active nodes and waits until active references drain before removal completes. This is a core-path fact, not proof that the module releases its separately mapped resources.

For a single sysfs_create_group failure, create_files removes files already created from the group; internal_create_group also removes a named group directory on error. The attribute-file rollback is provided by pinned sysfs core; module-specific mapping and OF-reference cleanup remain separate.

inferences.claim: On the stock success path where of_find_compatible_node returns a node, the missing of_node_put is consistent with an outstanding device_node reference. This is a statically supported possible reference-retention issue; do not report a runtime leak without L4 confirmation of the target path and teardown context.

If platform_device_register fails after device_initialize, pinned API documentation requires platform_device_put. No such call exists in the stock function corpus; exact residual refcount/release behavior for this module object needs L4 review.

If platform_device_register succeeds but __platform_driver_probe finds no bound device, the pinned core unregisters only the driver and returns -ENODEV; init failure frees module memory without calling cleanup_module. Because the registered ftm_dev object is in module .data, this creates a possible stale registered-device pointer/UAF risk. This is a risk hypothesis requiring L4/core-path review, not a claim of observed runtime UAF.
